evidence.text: Analyzes 您 as 心 (semantic) + 你 (phonetic), a second-person pronoun. It quotes Jin 董解元《西廂記諸宮調》卷五 “您且聽着” and Yuan 白樸《梧桐雨》 “您眾軍” for plural use. The modern honorific example is from twentieth-century 楊沫《青春之歌》. These are the database’s cited examples; dates of the specific textual witnesses were not independently checked.
evidence.kind: character-specific dictionary analysis and quoted attestations
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 - 字頭「您」

evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.text: States 您 is not recorded in 說文, gives current Mandarin nín, and defines the pronoun as an honorific second-person form also used broadly for plural ‘you’. It cites a 五代史平話 example and a Yuan 張國賓《合汗衫》 example. This establishes dictionary-reported usage and does not explain the graph’s formation.
evidence.title: [A01365] 您 - 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.text: For 您, the database explicitly identifies 你 as the sound component. Its separate entry for 你 says it is a pronoun meaning second-person singular, absent from oracle-bone and bronze inscriptions and 說文; it cites 《集韻·止韻》 “你，汝也” and 《隋書·李密傳》. The two entries do not give historical reconstructions demonstrating how the sounds matched when 您 was formed.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 - 字頭「你」

evidence.text: The file description calls the image a computer-font reconstruction of 你 in Small Seal style and says the character did not historically exist in seal script. It is explicitly a modern reconstruction, not an ancient artifact image. The inspected description page links the original image and states public-domain status as ineligible for copyright.

gaps: The source material directly supports a phonetic role for 你 and semantic role for 心 in the present graph, but this pass did not find paleographic forms for 您 or establish when that compound spelling arose. Do not infer ancient composition from the modern parts.

The competing lexical derivations summarized in the dossier—plural contraction (你們/你每), 你老 contraction, or a relation to Buddhist 仁—were not independently adjudicated in this invocation. The specific historical source word for the early 您/恁 form and the sound match needed for each contraction remain unsettled.

CUHK’s cited Jin and Yuan works provide early quoted uses, including a plural example, but the manuscript or edition dates and the alleged Tang/Five Dynasties occurrence/corruption were not checked against primary witnesses here. The honorific development’s chronology remains unresolved.

No historical sound reconstructions for 您 and 你 were obtained in this pass. A component reading cannot be substituted with the host reading; modern readings and the database’s sound-role claim do not establish the historical sound relation.
The Commons candidate is a modern reconstruction of the 你 component, not an attested form of 您. No historic glyph image for 您 with identity and reuse provenance was verified, so no image is proposed.
The official Unicode character-specific Unihan pages and exact local Unihan rows were not checked in this invocation; current kMandarin click-through evidence is therefore not added.
